title: Maa Bhagwati Rice Industries And Another v. State of U.P. And 7 Others
coram: Manoj Misra, J. & Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Notice issued; Clause 4.3(iv) vires not decided; writ pending
headnote: Where purchasers of the assets of a company in liquidation, who say they are not bound to pay that company's electricity dues, are refused a fresh connection because those dues remain outstanding, and they challenge Clause 4.3(iv) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 — under which outstanding dues of a connection provided to a company are a first charge on its assets — as not contemplated by the Electricity Act, 2003, as beyond delegated legislation, and as violating Article 300-A, the Court records that the matter requires consideration, issues notice including to the Advocate General, and calls for counters. A later modification application offering a bank guarantee pending the vires challenge was listed for instructions and was not decided. Subsequent sheets only adjourn. Clause 4.3(iv) is not construed, no connection is directed, and the writ remains pending.
facts:
Maa Bhagwati Rice Industries and another claim to have purchased the assets of respondent no. 6, a company in liquidation, and thereby to have become owners of the property. They say they are not otherwise bound to pay that company's electricity dues. A fresh electricity connection was nonetheless not being provided because those predecessor dues remained unpaid.

They questioned the validity of Clause 4.3(iv) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, under which outstanding dues of a connection provided to a company are a first charge on the company's assets, as a charge not contemplated by the Electricity Act, 2003, as beyond the power of delegated legislation unless specifically conferred by statute, and as violating Article 300-A of the Constitution. On a modification application they offered a bank guarantee so as not to lose their money if the clause were struck down.

holding_units.clause: 4.3(iv) as cited (electricity dues of a company-consumer as a first charge on its assets)
holding_units.topic: vires challenge to the first-charge clause by a purchaser of liquidation assets refused a new connection for predecessor dues; notice issued, not decided
holding_units.question: May a purchaser of a company in liquidation's assets obtain a fresh connection without discharging that company's electricity dues, on the ground that Clause 4.3(iv) of the Supply Code, creating a first charge on the company's assets, is ultra vires the Electricity Act, 2003 and Article 300-A?
holding_units.holding: Not decided on merits. Recording that the petitioners, purchasers of a company in liquidation's assets, claimed they were not bound to pay that company's electricity dues, and that they challenged Clause 4.3(iv) as creating a first charge not contemplated by the Electricity Act, 2003 and as violating Article 300-A, the Court held that the matter required consideration, issued notice including to the Advocate General, and called for counters. A modification application offering a bank guarantee pending the vires challenge was listed for the licensee's instructions and was not ruled on. Later sheets granted further time for a counter and, on 26.8.2022, listed the matter before the appropriate Bench as relating to grant of an electricity connection. Clause 4.3(iv) was not construed and no connection was directed.

principle_tags.application: The writ attacks Clause 4.3(iv) of the 2005 Code, described as making outstanding dues of a company-consumer a first charge on its assets, as ultra vires the Electricity Act, 2003 and Article 300-A. Notice issued; the first-charge clause was not construed.

A fresh connection was withheld from purchasers of a company in liquidation's assets because that company's electricity dues remained unpaid. The petitioners claimed they were not bound to pay those dues; the Court issued notice and did not direct a connection.

After admission, notice to the Advocate General, an undecided bank-guarantee offer, and adjournments, the last sheet listed the writ before the appropriate Bench as relating to grant of an electricity connection. Clause 4.3(iv) remains unadjudicated.
